tasks.short: Prepare and give court testimony about investigation findings.

steps.what: Agree testimony scope and hearing arrangements with legal counsel.
Locate exhibits and reconcile references to investigation records.
Prepare a factual chronology and notes explaining methods, findings, and limitations.

loop.input: Approved findings and indexed exhibits within the testimony scope.
loop.output: Draft chronology and method notes with exhibit references.
loop.check: Check dates and figures against records; investigator verifies every factual assertion and limitation.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per pack; unresolved claims return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the pack but cannot explain varied investigative methods and limitations.

steps.what: Review permissible disclosures and practise answering questions with legal counsel.
Give evidence and answer questions in court.
Record hearing outcomes and requests for further evidence.

tasks.design: A generator on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles exhibit references from the evidence register and records in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares source-linked notes, while configured forms in {PROJECT} capture hearing follow-ups. Legal counsel reviews disclosures; the investigator prepares personally and gives testimony.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exhibit links, versions, and access permissions were inconsistent. Generic drafting tools lacked dependable references.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable evidence identifiers and templates support automated assembly. AI-assisted coding reduces implementation effort, and bounded drafting can explain source-linked material.
tasks.still_hard: Admissibility, disclosure limits, disputed interpretations, and live questioning require people. GDPR, the EU AI Act where applicable, and national procedural rules constrain use.
tasks.human_edge: The witness explains what they actually observed, admits uncertainty, and responds under questioning.
tasks.altitude: The investigator spends less preparation time finding exhibits and more time testing explanations with legal counsel. Testimony responsibilities and decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Prepare source-linked workpapers supporting disputed findings.
reach.learn: Learn evidence provenance, version control, and how to distinguish observations from conclusions.

evidence.claim: Evidence retrieval and referenced workpapers are established automation capabilities; court admissibility is a separate question.
Baker Tilly Netherlands reported faster statement checks and tests of details; these results do not measure testimony preparation.
Giving testimony and answering contested questions remain human work.

assumptions: Shares describe active work, excluding travel and waiting at court.
The investigator is a factual witness; specialist expert-witness duties may require additional steps.
Estimates cover one testimony-pack pilot using an existing evidence register.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether exhibits have stable identifiers and retained original versions.
Which records legal counsel permits in the drafting environment.
Required exhibit formats and filing procedures.
Available access to investigation records and hearing outcomes.
research_questions: Which national procedural rules govern computer-generated preparation materials and exhibit provenance?
Which controls best detect unsupported statements in a testimony draft?
new_work: Resolve broken references and version conflicts.
Maintain pack templates, permissions, and generation logs.
Check that preparation notes preserve uncertainty and do not reshape witness recollection.

tasks.short: Investigate suspicious financial activity and recommend a supported resolution.

steps.what: Review the allegation and agree investigation scope, urgency, and authorised access.
Retrieve relevant transactions, claims, supplier records, and bank records within authorised scope.
Register evidence, preserve originals, and record collection details.
Match transactions and test duplicates, unusual timing, amounts, and counterparty links.
Read correspondence and contracts to build a chronology and identify evidence gaps.

loop.input: Authorised correspondence and contracts linked to registered evidence.
loop.output: Source-linked events, explicit dates, conflicting accounts, and possible evidence gaps.
loop.check: Verify citations, entities, and dates; investigator reviews conflicts and rejects inferred facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting records remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant events occur in varied free text; fixed field mappings cannot capture them reliably.

steps.what: Interview relevant people and obtain accounts addressing evidence gaps.
Evaluate competing explanations and write findings with recommended next actions.
Review findings and authorise closure, further investigation, or escalation.

tasks.design: Scoped integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieve records from {ERP}, {EXPENSE}, {PROCUREMENT}, and {BANK}; configured records in {DOCS} retain provenance and originals. Deterministic checks feed a {BI} view, and a bounded extraction loop drafts a chronology with source references. Investigators conduct interviews and decide what the evidence supports; a {WORKFLOW} approval records the authorised disposition.
tasks.previous_blocker: Investigators assembled records across separate permissions and identifiers. Narrative evidence and competing explanations resisted fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, configurable records, and deterministic matching support much of the work. Bounded extraction can reduce reading effort without deciding guilt or closing cases.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence, identity ambiguity, deliberate concealment, and fair interpretation remain expensive. GDPR and EU AI Act applicability require assessment; national rules govern employee investigations and consultation.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator tests innocent explanations, conducts fair interviews, and judges whether evidence supports an allegation.

ambition.what: Monthly approval of targeted payment-control changes from recurring investigation findings.

tasks.altitude: The investigator spends less time assembling records and more time resolving conflicting evidence and advising finance leaders. A delegated mandate could add authority to propose scoped control trials; case closure and external reporting retain their existing approval rights.

reach.task: Assess recurring fraud patterns and recommend control changes.
reach.learn: Learn control effectiveness testing, false-positive measurement, and residual-risk assessment.

reach.task: Build transaction exception views with traceable source records.
reach.learn: Learn entity matching, access controls, and evidence-preserving data lineage.

evidence.claim: Hawk combines transaction-monitoring rules and machine learning with alert reasons and four-eye review.
The Dutch fraud-list case documents serious harm from unlawful personal-data processing; it does not validate investigation automation.
In the Netherlands, staff-monitoring arrangements can require works council consent under article 27.
An ordinary company should not assume that regulated-sector suspicious-transaction reporting duties apply to it.

assumptions: This is a corporate finance investigation team, not necessarily a regulated financial institution.
The evidence register is configured using existing retention, versioning, and access features.
Retrieval follows an approved scope; integrations do not grant new investigative access.
Estimates cover a pilot with a limited set of financial data feeds and document types.
Shares differ from the priors because financial matching and explicit case approval are separate activities.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether the company is subject to sector-specific reporting obligations.
Countries involved and applicable employee consultation arrangements.
Existing case-record and evidence-preservation capabilities.
Availability and quality of transaction exports and counterparty identifiers.
Authorised access to correspondence, employee records, and bank data.
Who can approve disposition, control trials, and external escalation.
research_questions: Which national rules govern employee evidence collection, interviews, and monitoring?
Which matching methods best expose ambiguous identities without treating similarity as proof?
How should evidence extraction be evaluated for omitted exculpatory material?
new_work: Review ambiguous transaction matches and extraction errors.
Check that favourable and contradictory evidence remains visible.
Maintain connectors, control rules, access scopes, and retention settings.
Monitor alert quality and document reasons for case dispositions.
Resolve missing records and failed imports.

tasks.short: Teach colleagues to recognise fraud indicators and use prevention and reporting procedures.

steps.what: Agree learning needs and select relevant, anonymised examples.
Write exercises, guidance, and knowledge checks for the selected audience.

loop.input: Training brief, approved anonymised examples, and current reporting procedures.
loop.output: Audience-specific exercises, explanations, and answer keys.
loop.check: Verify every procedure against its source; trainer checks realism and answers for ambiguity.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per module; unsupported advice is removed or written manually.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure but adapting scenarios and explanations to different roles needs writing.

steps.what: Approve examples and advice for internal release.
Schedule sessions, enrol learners, and send preparation materials.
Run exercises, discuss concerns, and explain appropriate escalation.
Record attendance and knowledge-check results in the learning system.
Review learner results and decide what needs reinforcement.

tasks.design: A bounded drafting loop turns approved material in {DOCS} into role-specific exercises and answer keys. Configured {LMS} workflows handle enrolment, invitations, fixed-answer scoring, and completion records, with {CALENDAR} supporting live sessions. A person approves release and leads discussion, while learning results inform reinforcement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation depended on specialist writing and repeated administration. Sensitive case examples could not be reused freely.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning workflows already cover administration. Approved, anonymised examples give bounded drafting a useful and controlled input.
tasks.still_hard: Anonymisation can fail in small teams. Building trust, correcting misconceptions, and teaching judgement remain human work; GDPR and national employee rules govern learner data.
tasks.human_edge: The trainer makes it safe to raise concerns and explains how to respond without making unsupported accusations.

ambition.what: Fraud scenario workshops for purchasing approvers.

tasks.altitude: The investigator can spend preparation time on realistic exercises and difficult questions. With an agreed mandate, they can choose reinforcement topics and adapt exercises; approval of policy advice remains with the compliance officer.

reach.task: Recognise invoice warning signs and route concerns through the reporting procedure.
reach.learn: Learn invoice-processing controls and the practical constraints of high-volume clerical work.

reach.task: Translate investigation lessons into usable reporting guidance.
reach.learn: Learn instructional design, anonymisation, and how to assess understanding through scenarios.

evidence.claim: Configured learning systems can manage enrolment, assessments, and completion records.
Bounded drafting can assist training preparation, but the digest contains no direct fraud-training deployment case.
Personalised examples and live discussion require review for confidentiality, accuracy, and audience needs.

assumptions: An existing {LMS} supports enrolment, fixed-answer checks, and completion capture.
The pilot covers one audience and one approved module.
Live discussions remain a substantial part of the training.
The consent and access range includes learner-data review and consultation where national rules require it.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Whether purchasing approvers already receive scenario-based fraud training.
Available anonymised examples and their release authority.
Current {LMS} features and permitted integration access.
Languages, accessibility needs, and learner-data retention rules.
Whether the investigator may independently choose reinforcement topics.
research_questions: Which scenario formats improve fraud recognition without encouraging indiscriminate suspicion?
How can anonymised examples be checked for re-identification through contextual details?
new_work: Review exercises and answer keys before release.
Maintain procedure references and module versions.
Use feedback to revise weak explanations.

tasks.short: Track fraud trends and assess their relevance to current controls and investigations.

steps.what: Check regulator notices, professional publications, and subscribed alerts.
Read updates, remove repetitions, and note useful claims and references.

loop.input: Deduplicated material from approved sources, with publication dates and references.
loop.output: Cited claims, fraud methods, affected processes, and explicit source limitations.
loop.check: Verify quoted support and dates; analyst checks important claims against original material.
loop.stop: One pass and one correction per item; inaccessible or unsupported items remain links for manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact deduplication is deterministic, but varied prose needs extraction to produce useful summaries.

steps.what: Compare credible developments with company exposures and decide what merits attention.
Discuss uncertain developments and practical implications with professional peers.
Record lessons and prepare proposed control or training updates.
Approve internal guidance and route proposals to the responsible control owner.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects permitted updates from {GOV_PORTAL}, subscribed {EMAIL} alerts, and professional publication sites represented by {OTHER}. Deterministic deduplication and a bounded extraction loop prepare cited briefs in {DOCS}, while configured templates carry analyst assessments into proposals. A {WORKFLOW} approval routes published guidance and control-review requests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful information was scattered across subscriptions and publication sites. Summaries needed specialist reading and could lose the source's qualifications.
tasks.enabler_now: Feed collection and deduplication are established techniques. Bounded extraction can organise free text while retaining references and uncertainty.
tasks.still_hard: Source credibility, local relevance, emerging methods, and misleading claims remain judgement problems. Licensing limits collection, and public information may still contain personal data subject to GDPR.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst distinguishes an interesting story from a credible threat to the company's actual processes.

ambition.what: Monthly selection of one emerging fraud method for a control tabletop review.

tasks.altitude: The analyst spends less time scanning and more time testing relevance with process owners. A delegated mandate could let them convene monthly tabletop reviews; authority to change controls remains with the responsible owner.

reach.task: Translate emerging fraud methods into process-specific exposure assessments.
reach.learn: Learn scenario design, control mapping, and how to distinguish exposure from observed incidents.

reach.task: Assess whether new notices require changes to internal guidance.
reach.learn: Learn legal-source hierarchy, jurisdiction checks, and effective-date tracking.

evidence.claim: Scheduled feeds, deterministic deduplication, and source-linked briefs are technically feasible without autonomous agents.
The digest contains no documented deployment measuring fraud-trend monitoring savings.
Professional learning requires assessment of credibility and relevance, beyond producing summaries.

assumptions: In the collection step, {OTHER} means professional publication websites and feeds.
Collection is limited to approved sources with permitted access.
Peer discussions use public or authorised information.
Estimates cover a small source set and one recurring brief.
The priors overstate automation of learning if collection is treated as equivalent to understanding.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
unknowns: Current subscriptions, approved sources, and collection permissions.
Which business processes and jurisdictions need coverage.
Who approves guidance and owns control changes.
Whether a monthly tabletop review already exists.
Access to the control inventory and approved investigation findings.
research_questions: Which source types give the earliest reliable signals for corporate payment and expense fraud?
How can summary quality be measured for missing qualifications and outdated claims?
Which tabletop formats help process owners assess emerging fraud methods?
new_work: Maintain source lists, credentials, and topic filters.
Review important claims and publication dates.
Resolve duplicate stories and conflicting reports.
Monitor collection failures and licensing changes.
Track whether proposed reviews produced useful control decisions.

role.altitude: The week shifts from finding records and preparing routine material toward interviews, evidence interpretation, teaching, and control advice. New rights require a specific delegated mandate, such as convening control reviews; testimony, case disposition, and external reporting retain their established responsibilities.
reach: Financial Risk Specialists: turn recurring findings into tested control proposals.
Accountants and Auditors: strengthen source-linked evidence and workpaper quality.
Business Intelligence Analysts: build traceable transaction exception views.
Compliance Officers: translate reliable findings into clear guidance.
skills_to_grow: Deterministic control design and false-positive measurement.
Bounded extraction evaluation, including omitted exculpatory evidence.
GDPR, EU AI Act applicability, and relevant national investigation rules.
role.ambitious_version: A fraud investigator who combines rigorous casework with a monthly control-learning service: select a credible emerging method, test it with a process owner, and present an evidence-backed control proposal for approval.
